sensitive_terms: A pure-Python, bring-your-own-I/O implementation of HTTP/1.1
This is a little HTTP/1.1 library written from scratch in Python

runner.install_command: export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3-pip && printf '[global]\nbreak-system-packages = true\n' > /etc/pip.conf && python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages --disable-pip-version-check 'setuptools==75.8.0' 'pytest==8.3.5' 'pytest-cov==6.0.0' && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
runner.env_probe_command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "import os; import httpwire; assert os.path.realpath(httpwire.__file__).startswith(os.path.realpath('httpwire')); client = httpwire.Connection(httpwire.CLIENT); wire = client.send(httpwire.Request(method='GET', target='/probe', headers=[('Host', 'localhost')])); assert wire.startswith(b'GET /probe HTTP/1.1'); assert client.send(httpwire.EndOfMessage()) == b''; server = httpwire.Connection(httpwire.SERVER); server.receive_data(wire); event = server.next_event(); assert type(event) is httpwire.Request and event.method == b'GET' and event.target == b'/probe'"

init_metadata.tech_stack: Pure Python bring-your-own-I/O HTTP/1.1 protocol state machine (setuptools flat layout, zero runtime deps, pytest); CPU-only

hardware_requirements.summary: This is a pure-Python library that encodes high-level HTTP request and response events into on-the-wire bytes and parses incoming bytes back into events, without performing any network I/O of its own. It has no compiled extensions, native code, or GPU/accelerator requirements, and zero declared runtime dependencies. The documented interpreter floor is Python 3.8 or newer. Any standard x86_64 or arm64 Linux, macOS, or Windows host with a supported interpreter is sufficient to install from source and run the test suite.

profiles.label: CPU baseline
profiles.description: Standard CPU-only Python execution path. Core capability is encoding a client-role HTTP/1.1 request event from this repository's source tree into on-the-wire bytes.
probes: cd /opt/codingbench/repo && PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "import httpwire, os; assert os.path.realpath(httpwire.__file__).startswith(os.path.realpath('httpwire')); conn = httpwire.Connection(our_role=httpwire.CLIENT); data = conn.send(httpwire.Request(method='GET', target='/', headers=[('Host', 'example.com')])); assert data.startswith(b'GET / HTTP/1.1')"
profiles.setup_notes: setup.py python_requires >=3.8 and declares no install_requires. Classifiers list CPython 3.8-3.12 and PyPy. tox envlist is format, py38-py312/pypy3, mypy; testenv deps are pytest and pytest-cov from test-requirements.txt; commands are pytest --cov=httpwire --cov-config=.coveragerc httpwire. CI on ubuntu-latest runs tox across CPython 3.8-3.13 and PyPy 3.9/3.10. CONTRIBUTING.md documents pip install tox && tox. No system libraries beyond a normal Python toolchain.
profiles.build_notes: No compiled/native build step. Packaging uses setuptools via setup.py (find_packages(exclude=['httpwire.tests'])). The importable package lives at the repository root (flat layout). Documented install: pip install httpwire. Editable install: pip install -e . CI uses tox which installs the package into each env.
